en: Mount Mayon in Albay is famous for its nearly perfect conical shape.
The Philippine eagle is a critically endangered bird species endemic to the tropical forests of the Philippines.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, flowing northward through the Cagayan Valley.
Taal Lake in Batangas is the third largest lake in the Philippines and contains Volcano Island.
Mount Pulag in Benguet is the highest peak in Luzon and is famous for its sea of clouds.
Palawan is the largest island province in the Philippines and features the Puerto Princesa Subterranean River.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO World Heritage site protecting marine biodiversity.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park contains an eight-kilometer underground river that flows directly into the sea.
Taal Volcano in Batangas is a complex volcano with a main crater lake located on Volcano Island.
The Waling-waling, scientifically known as Vanda sanderiana, is a rare orchid species endemic to the island of Mindanao.
The Cordillera Administrative Region in northern Luzon contains the Banaue Rice Terraces, which are carved into the mountains.
The San Bernardino Strait is a body of water that separates the Bicol Region of Luzon from Eastern Visayas.
